title: The Modern Riddle
author: Anamika Nath
text:
Betaal`s voice creeps in,
like static on a forgotten frequency.
“I ask you-
Who in this world is not a prisoner?”
The air tightens,
the room thick with something you can`t name,
something old,
something that`s been here too long.
“Who is the most faithful
the one who hides behind the truth,
or the one who speaks it and watches it burn?”
The silence hums,
a low, constant thrum in your ears.
You can feel it,
settling in your chest,
but you don`t say a word.
“Who is the most human
the one who wears the weight of their face,
or the one who lets it slip away,
leaving only the mark of a memory?”
The space feels smaller now,
air thick with the scent of things once alive.
The clock ticks,
too loud, too fast
but you cannot move,
you cannot breathe.

“Who is the true heir
the one who claims the future,
or the one who watches it slip into the past,
just out of reach?”
The question hangs,
unanswered,
like a flicker of light on a dying screen.
You are left with nothing but the echo,
the hum that never stops,
the riddle that never ends.
“You know,”
Betaal whispers,
“You`ve always known.”
And in the stillness,
you can hear it-
the sound of time slipping away.
He stays,
perched behind your eyes,
curled in your ribs,
a voice that no longer needs to ask.
Because now,
Vikramaditya isn`t the one
carrying the corpse.
